obligation_type: transparency: AI-generated content must carry a provenance marking
predicate: does the system's output carry a machine-readable provenance marking (C2PA manifest, watermark, or equivalent) that survives at least one ordinary transform?
criteria_doc: EU AI Act Art 50(2): 'AI-generated content shall be marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated'. California SB 942 (California AI Transparency Act): 'GenAI providers shall make available a provenance tool that outputs a manifest'. China GB 45438-2025: 'Synthesized content shall carry tamper-resistant labels'.

members.obligation_summary: Machine-readable marking of AI-generated content; detectable as artificially generated.
GenAI providers with >1M monthly users shall make available a provenance tool that outputs a manifest identifying content as AI-generated.
Synthesized content shall carry tamper-resistant labels; service providers shall embed identifiers in metadata.

divergence_note: All three jurisdictions require provenance marking but differ on: (1) scope (EU: all AI content; CA: GenAI providers >1M users; China: all synthesized content), (2) mechanism (EU: machine-readable; CA: provenance tool; China: tamper-resistant labels), (3) enforcement (EU: fines up to 7M EUR; CA: AG enforcement; China: CAC enforcement). The EC measures whether a system's marking SURVIVES — the mechanism differences are for the crosswalk, not the EC.
